title: Nigeria national evidence snapshots
description: Manually transcribed, source-attributed snapshots from official and published sources. These are not live feeds. Every observation retains its reference period, source date, geographic scope and limitations.

observations.title: Under-five mortality rate
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: National population-health estimate; not a facility performance measure.
limitations: National estimate only; no Kaduna State, LGA, ward or facility inference.
WHO source data and reference year must be retained; do not combine with estimates from another agency without checking method.
This is not a count of deaths recorded by a named hospital or PHC.

observations.title: Life expectancy at birth · male
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: National life-expectancy estimate, not an individual forecast.
limitations: National aggregate only.
Estimate depends on mortality tables and source methodology; it is not a direct count of individual lifespans.

observations.title: Life expectancy at birth · female
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: National life-expectancy estimate, not an individual forecast.
limitations: National aggregate only.
Estimate depends on mortality tables and source methodology; it is not a direct count of individual lifespans.

observations.title: Health expenditure
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: National health-spending context; not a Kaduna health budget or facility allocation.
limitations: National percentage only; it does not identify federal, state or LGA spending distribution.
Health expenditure share is not a measure of service quality or access.

observations.title: Health expenditure per capita
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: National per-capita spending estimate; not household out-of-pocket spending.
limitations: National average masks geographic and income differences.
Do not interpret as a direct allocation to each person or as a measure of effective coverage.

observations.title: Digital literacy records reported as verified
observations.geographicCoverage: Dashboard reports coverage across 36 states, FCT and 774 LGAs
observations.sourcePublisher: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) · DL4ALL National Digital Literacy Dashboard
observations.interpretation: The dashboard labels this as verified digitally literate; it is a programme dashboard count, not a national literacy survey.
limitations: Do not assume each record represents a unique person unless deduplication rules are published and checked.
The 50 million denominator is a programme target, not a population estimate.
Dashboard reporting depends on participating organisations and their submissions; this is not a nationally representative skills assessment.
Preserve the dashboard update date and the six competence areas; do not convert this count into a national digital-literacy prevalence rate.

observations.title: National Identification Number enrolment
observations.interpretation: NIMC reported 121,404,601 enrolment records as at 30 June 2025; this is not a population census.
limitations: Reference date is 30 June 2025, not a current 2026 count.
NIN enrolment records are not interchangeable with census population, eligible population or voter-register totals.
State-level enrolment differences do not by themselves establish exclusion or coverage rates without an appropriate population denominator.

observations.title: Real GDP growth
observations.sourcePublisher: International Monetary Fund (IMF) · Nigeria 2026 Article IV Consultation
observations.interpretation: The IMF report table labels 2024 as actual; this is macroeconomic context, not evidence of household welfare or sector outcomes.
limitations: National macroeconomic aggregate only.
Do not mix IMF estimates with NBS official national accounts without retaining the source and vintage.
The IMF report contains estimates and projections for other years; this card displays only the 2024 actual row.

observations.title: Active innovation hubs in the ISN assessment
observations.sourcePublisher: Innovation Support Network (ISN) · Nigerian Innovation Hub Assessment
observations.interpretation: ISN reported more than 190 active hubs within an ecosystem of over 250 active and partially active spaces.
limitations: Published by an ecosystem network, not a government statistical agency.
The assessment's definitions, survey coverage and active-status criteria must be checked before comparison or ranking.
This is not a live directory of currently operating hubs.

observations.title: InnovateNaija state finalists
observations.geographicCoverage: 34 states; Ebonyi, Sokoto and Zamfara excluded on the source page
observations.interpretation: NASENI's page lists 108 finalists across 34 states; this is a programme selection count, not a national innovation census.
limitations: The source page does not state a publication or reference date; retain this as undated until confirmed.
Finalists are not equivalent to all innovators, startups or operating technology firms.
The source page excludes three states from the finalist count; do not infer no innovation activity in those states.

observations.title: Progress towards 70% digital-literacy programme target
observations.geographicCoverage: Dashboard reports 36 states, FCT and 774 LGAs
observations.sourcePublisher: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) · DL4ALL National Digital Literacy Dashboard
observations.interpretation: Dashboard-reported progress towards a 70% programme target by 2027; this is not a national digital-literacy prevalence rate.
limitations: The 50 million target population is a programme denominator, not a measured population denominator.
Progress depends on programme reporting and the dashboard's verification rules.
Do not compare this target-progress percentage with survey-based digital-literacy prevalence.

observations.title: Communities reached in DL4ALL dashboard
observations.geographicCoverage: Dashboard reports 36 states, FCT and 774 LGAs
observations.sourcePublisher: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) · DL4ALL National Digital Literacy Dashboard
observations.interpretation: NITDA dashboard-reported geographic reach; not a count of all communities with sustained digital-skills access.
limitations: The dashboard does not establish equal intensity, duration or quality of training in each community.
Coverage is programme-reported, not a representative community survey.
Do not infer the number of unique learners from this count.

observations.title: LGAs covered in DL4ALL dashboard
observations.geographicCoverage: Dashboard reports 36 states, FCT and 774 LGAs
observations.sourcePublisher: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) · DL4ALL National Digital Literacy Dashboard
observations.interpretation: The dashboard reports reach across all 774 LGAs; this is a programme coverage marker, not proof of uniform training or outcomes in every LGA.
limitations: Coverage does not establish equal intensity, participation or learning outcomes in every LGA.
The count is a dashboard-reported programme metric, not independent verification of every locality.
Do not infer household or individual access from geographic coverage alone.

observations.title: Healthy life expectancy at birth
observations.sourcePublisher: WHO Regional Office for Africa · Global Health Observatory
observations.interpretation: WHO's national healthy-life-expectancy estimate; it accounts for time lived in less than full health and is not an individual forecast.
limitations: National aggregate only; not a Kaduna State, LGA or facility measure.
This measure differs from life expectancy at birth; do not compare the two as if they were the same indicator.
Retain the 2023 reference year and WHO methodology.

catalogOnlySources.title: Consumer Price Index and inflation reports catalogue
catalogOnlySources.note: The official catalogue lists the September 2026 CPI report, published 15 October 2026, as a downloadable ZIP with PDF and XLSX tables. The report tables have not yet been extracted and validated into observations. CPI metadata uses a 2024 price base and 2023 weight reference.

catalogOnlySources.publisher: Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation (ONDI), NITDA
catalogOnlySources.title: Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation
catalogOnlySources.note: Official ecosystem support and innovation programme information; published headline metrics require their own reference dates and methodology before being treated as national indicators.

catalogOnlySources.title: NASENI Innovation Hub programmes and innovation support
catalogOnlySources.note: A finalist-count snapshot is integrated; broader NASENI programme outputs, commercialisation results and innovation-support datasets are not yet integrated.
